title: Testing Asynchronous Applications
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of testing asynchronous applications in a FastAPI application.
Apply or interpret one example related to async test functions.
Identify one limitation or failure case and describe how to verify it.

content.intro: This lesson covers testing asynchronous applications within testing and code quality. Use the supplied syllabus topics as the coverage checklist, then connect them to the worked example and the verification task.
content.why_it_matters: You will use testing asynchronous applications to build APIs whose contracts and behavior are understandable to both clients and maintainers. The practical aim is resource lifecycle, cancellation, concurrency limits and observable I/O behavior.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: Testing Asynchronous Applications matters because it is part of testing and code quality. In practice, focus on resource lifecycle, cancellation, concurrency limits and observable I/O behavior. A framework feature only helps when its assumptions match the application; keep input validation, business policy and side effects distinguishable.

items.title: Async test functions
items.text: Use async test functions to make behavior observable and repeatable. Specify one normal case, one invalid or missing-input case, and the expected status or diagnostic. A passing happy path alone is not enough evidence.

items.title: HTTPX async clients
items.text: For httpx async clients, identify which operation waits on I/O, which resources remain open, and what happens on timeout or disconnect. Async syntax does not make CPU-bound work faster or durable background jobs reliable by itself.

items.title: ASGI transport
items.text: Use asgi transport as a design decision rather than a keyword to memorize. State the input and expected result, identify the boundary conditions, and connect the concept to the surrounding FastAPI request lifecycle.

content_blocks.title: Worked example: Testing Asynchronous Applications
content_blocks.code:
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from fastapi import FastAPI

@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI):
    app.state.ready = True
    yield
    app.state.ready = False

app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)
content_blocks.expected_output: The lifespan setup runs before requests are served and cleanup runs at shutdown.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Run locally and watch startup/shutdown logs; do not use this example to store secrets in code.
content_blocks.reset_steps: For read-only examples, no reset is needed. For any example that writes state, use a disposable local database/test fixture; record the starting state and clean up only lab data. Never use production credentials or real personal data.

expected_output: A reviewable example or design note for Testing Asynchronous Applications, covering the PDF subtopics, expected behavior and at least one verification check.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a code fragment without checking its assumptions.
common_mistakes.why: Installed versions, imported types, application structure and external services affect behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: State assumptions; check the versioned official docs; run a minimal local test and add one failure case.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating one happy-path response as proof of correctness.
common_mistakes.why: Invalid input, permissions, concurrency, timeouts and cleanup are not exercised by a single request.
common_mistakes.fix: Add focused normal and negative tests and record exact expected status/body.

common_mistakes.why: Even short examples may mutate records, reveal data or affect availability.
common_mistakes.fix: Use synthetic inputs and a disposable environment; review security, cleanup and rollback before promotion.
